title: Vowel Harmony and Consonant Assimilation
subtitle: The foundational sound rules governing all Kazakh suffixes
keyPoint: Kazakh suffixes must match the stem's front/back vowel quality and adjust their initial consonants based on whether the preceding sound is voiced, unvoiced, or a vowel.

cells: п, ф, к, қ, т, с, ш, щ, х, ц, ч, һ
ж, з, м, н, ң, л, р, й, у

mistakes.note: 'Бала' contains back vowels (а), so it requires the back vowel variant -лар.
After the voiceless consonant 'п', the suffix must begin with the voiceless consonant 'т'.
'Көз' ends in the voiced consonant 'з' and has a front vowel (ө), requiring -дер.

quiz.question: Choose the correct plural form of 'кітап' (book):
quiz.explanation: 'Кітап' ends in voiceless 'п' and has back vowels, requiring -тар.

quiz.question: Choose the correct plural form of 'үй' (house):
quiz.explanation: 'Үй' ends in semivowel 'й' and contains front vowel 'ү', taking -лер.

quiz.question: Choose the correct plural form of 'қалам' (pen):
quiz.explanation: 'Қалам' ends in sonorant 'м' and has back vowels, taking -дар.

quiz.question: Choose the correct plural form of 'сөз' (word):
quiz.explanation: 'Сөз' contains front vowel 'ө' and voiced 'з', taking -дер.

tip: Look at the very last vowel of the stem to choose front vs. back, and the very last letter to choose the initial consonant of the suffix.

title: Spatial Cases: Locative, Dative, and Ablative
subtitle: Expressing location (at/in), destination (to), and origin (from)
keyPoint: Use the Locative (-да/-де/-та/-те) for 'at/in', Dative (-ға/-ге/-қа/-ке) for 'to/towards', and Ablative (-дан/-ден/-тан/-тен/-нан/-нен) for 'from'.

mistakes.note: Use Locative (-да), not Dative (-ға), for static living/residing.
Movement towards a destination takes Dative (-ге), not Ablative (-ден).
After voiceless 'п', the Locative suffix must be voiceless '-те'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Студент кітапхана___ отыр' (The student is sitting in the library).
quiz.explanation: Library takes Locative -да ('in/at the library').

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Біз ертең ауыл___ барамыз' (We are going to the village tomorrow).
quiz.explanation: Destination requires Dative -ға ('to the village').

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Ол жұмыс___ келді' (He came from work).
quiz.explanation: Origin after voiceless 'с' takes Ablative -тан ('from work').

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Айгүл дүкен___ нан алды' (Aygul bought bread from the shop).
quiz.explanation: After nasal 'н' in 'дүкен', Ablative uses -нен ('from the shop').

tip: Locative answers 'Қайда?' (Where?), Dative answers 'Қайда?' (Where to?), and Ablative answers 'Қайдан?' (From where?).

title: Possessive Suffixes and the Genitive Case
subtitle: Expressing 'my', 'your', and 'X of Y' relations
keyPoint: Possession requires attaching the Genitive case to the possessor and a matching possessive suffix to the possessed noun.

examples.en: Менің анам дәрігер болып жұмыс істейді.

mistakes.note: Kazakh requires the possessive suffix on the noun even when the pronoun 'менің' is present.
Third-person possession always requires -ы/-і/-сы/-сі on the possessed noun.
Second person singular takes -ың/-ің on the possessed item.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Менің қалам___ жоғалды' (My pen was lost).
quiz.explanation: 'Менің' (my) takes the 1st person suffix -ым on consonant-ending back-vowel stems.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Сенің үй___ қайда?' (Where is your house?).
quiz.explanation: 'Сенің' (your, informal) takes -ің on front-vowel stems ending in consonants.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Оның әке___ мұғалім' (His father is a teacher).
quiz.explanation: 'Әке' ends in a vowel, so third person takes -сі.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Айдос___ кітабы үстелде жатыр' (Aydos's book is on the table).
quiz.explanation: Aydos is the possessor, so voiceless ending 'с' requires Genitive -тың.

tip: Even if you omit the pronoun 'менің' or 'сенің', the suffix on the noun alone makes the owner 100% clear.

title: Existential Predicates: Бар and Жоқ
subtitle: Expressing 'there is', 'there isn't', and 'to have'
keyPoint: Kazakh expresses 'have/don't have' by attaching a possessive suffix to the noun and adding 'бар' (there is) or 'жоқ' (there is not).

cells: I have a car (My car exists).
I don't have time (My time does not exist).

mistakes.note: While 'Менде кітап бар' is sometimes heard colloquially, standard Kazakh uses the genitive + possessive: 'Менің кітабым бар'.
'Емес' negates adjectives and noun qualities ('not milk'); existential absence requires 'жоқ' ('no milk exists').
The noun must take the possessive suffix (-ым) before 'жоқ'.

quiz.question: How do you ask 'Do you have a question?' (informal):
quiz.explanation: Genitive 'Сенің' + possessive 'сұрағың' + 'бар ма?' correctly asks if you have a question.

quiz.question: Choose the correct translation: 'I don't have money':
quiz.explanation: 'Менің ақшам жоқ' literally means 'My money does not exist' = 'I have no money'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Үстелде қалам бар, бірақ дәптер ___' (There is a pen on the table, but no notebook).
quiz.explanation: Existential absence of the notebook requires 'жоқ'.

quiz.question: To negate 'Мұнда дәріхана бар' (There is a pharmacy here), you say:
quiz.explanation: The negative counterpart of 'бар' is 'жоқ'.

tip: Never confuse 'емес' (is not) with 'жоқ' (does not exist / don't have). 'Бұл алма емес' (This is not an apple) vs 'Алма жоқ' (There are no apples).

title: Present Actual Tense with Postural Auxiliaries
subtitle: Expressing actions happening right now via жатыр, отыр, тұр, and жүр
keyPoint: Continuous present actions right now are built by attaching converb -ып/-іп/-п to the main verb followed by a conjugated posture verb (жатыр, отыр, тұр, or жүр).

cells: actions in progress, resting, reading lying

mistakes.note: 'Оқимын' is simple present/future (I read/will read). Ongoing actions right now require the compound tense with 'жатыр'.
The main verb must take the converb suffix (-ып/-іп/-п) before the auxiliary.
Personal agreement suffixes must attach to the auxiliary verb (-мыз for 'біз').

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Мен қазір музыка тыңдап ___' (I am listening to music right now, sitting):
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular ('Мен') takes personal suffix -мын on the auxiliary verb: отырмын.

quiz.question: How do you say 'What are you doing right now?' (informal):
quiz.explanation: 'істеп жатырсың' is the present continuous form addressed to 'сен'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Оқушылар тақтаға қарап ___' (The students are looking at the blackboard, standing):
quiz.explanation: 3rd person plural / singular takes bare 'тұр' without extra personal suffixes.

quiz.question: What suffix connects the lexical verb stem to the postural auxiliary in Present Actual?
quiz.explanation: The converb suffix -ып/-іп/-п connects the main verb to the auxiliary (e.g., жаз + ып + отыр).

tip: 'Жатыр' is the most neutral auxiliary for ongoing events, while 'отыр', 'тұр', and 'жүр' preserve a subtle nuance of the subject's physical posture or mobility.

title: Nominal Predicates and Personal Clitics
subtitle: Forming 'to be' statements without an overt verb
keyPoint: Kazakh expresses identity and state by attaching personal agreement suffixes directly to nouns and adjectives without using an overt auxiliary verb.

useCases.label: Describing Physical or Emotional States
useCases.example: Біз шаршадық емес, біз бүгін дайынбыз.

mistakes.note: Do not insert forms of 'болу' (to be/become) for present tense stative sentences; attach personal endings directly to the noun.
Maintain vowel harmony and consonant assimilation: after sonorant consonants like 'м', use '-мін' instead of '-пын'.
Third-person singular takes no personal suffix in standard everyday Kazakh; avoid adding redundant endings.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Мен мұғалім___.' (I am a teacher.)
quiz.explanation: The first-person singular suffix after the soft sonorant 'м' is '-мін' due to vowel harmony and consonant voicing rules.

quiz.question: Choose the correct ending: 'Сен өте мейірімді___.' (You are very kind.)
quiz.explanation: 'Мейірімді' ends with a front vowel, so the informal second-person suffix takes the soft form '-сің'.

quiz.question: Select the correct form for 'We are ready': 'Біз дайын___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Дайын' ends with the consonant 'н' and has back vowels, requiring the first-person plural ending '-быз'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly says 'You (formal) are a doctor'?
quiz.explanation: The polite second-person singular pronoun 'Сіз' governs the predicate suffix '-сіз' (front vowel).

tip: Personal suffixes mirror the possessive and verbal agreement stems: check the final sound of the root to pick between nasal (м/н), voiced (б), or voiceless (п) variants.

title: Definite Accusative vs. Unmarked Direct Objects
subtitle: Distinguishing specific entities from general concepts
keyPoint: A direct object takes the accusative suffix (-ны/-ні, -ды/-ді, -ты/-ті, -н) only when it refers to a specific, definite item; generic non-specific objects stay in the bare nominative.

cells: I read a book / did book-reading.

examples.en: Мен мына қызықты кітапты сатып алдым.
Сіз бүгін таңертең шай іштіңіз бе?

mistakes.note: Generic consumable nouns without determiners should not take the accusative case.
Proper nouns are inherently definite and must take the accusative suffix when serving as direct objects.
Nouns with the third-person possessive suffix (-ы/-і/-сы/-сі) take the accusative marker '-н', not '-ны/-ні'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence for 'I drink water every day' (generic):
quiz.explanation: Generic direct objects in habitual actions remain in the bare nominative form without case markers.

quiz.question: Select the correct form: 'Give me that pen' -> 'Маған мына қалам___ берші.'
quiz.explanation: The demonstrative 'мына' makes the pen definite; 'қалам' ends in a voiced consonant 'м', requiring the accusative suffix '-ды'.

quiz.question: How do you correctly say 'Did you see his phone?' -> 'Сен оның телефонын___ көрдің бе?'
quiz.explanation: The third-person possessive form 'телефоны' already receives '-н' for the accusative ('телефонын'), so no further ending is added.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Мен сен___ жақсы түсінемін.' (I understand you well.)
quiz.explanation: Pronouns are definite; the accusative form of 'сен' is 'сені'.

tip: If you can place 'the' in front of the English noun, or if it is preceded by 'мына/анау' (this/that), you almost certainly need the accusative case.

title: Instrumental Case and Governed Postpositions
subtitle: Expressing accompaniment, instruments, and spatial relations
keyPoint: The instrumental suffix (-мен/-бен/-пен) marks tools and accompaniment, while postpositions dictate whether preceding nouns must take nominative, dative, or ablative cases.

mistakes.note: The postposition 'кейін' (after) strictly requires the preceding noun to take the ablative case (-дан/-ден/-тан/-тен).
The instrumental suffix is '-мен/-бен/-пен'; avoid duplicating syllables.
Use 'дейін' (or dialectal variants correctly harmonized): after a vowel or voiced consonant, 'дейін' is standard.

quiz.question: Which case does the postposition 'кейін' (after) govern?
quiz.explanation: 'Кейін' requires its argument to appear in the ablative case, as in 'шайдан кейін' (after tea).

quiz.question: Complete the phrase: 'Дос___ бірге киноға бардым.' (I went to the movies together with a friend.)
quiz.explanation: 'With my friend' combines possessive '-ым' and instrumental '-мен' -> 'досыммен'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct postposition: 'Үйге ___ жүгірдік.' (We ran towards the house.)
quiz.explanation: 'Қарай' (towards) governs the dative case ('үйге').

quiz.question: What is the proper instrumental ending for 'пышақ' (knife): 'Пышақ___ нанды кесті'?
quiz.explanation: Roots ending in voiceless consonants like 'қ' take the voiceless variant '-пен'.

tip: Remember: Kazakh has no prepositions. Suffixes attach directly to words, and standalone postposition words always follow the noun they govern.

title: Definite Witnessed Past Tense (-ды/-ді)
subtitle: Describing actions personally seen, verified, or definitively finished
keyPoint: The definite past tense suffix (-ды/-ді, -ты/-ті) attaches to verb stems and uses short personal endings (-м, -ң, -ңыз, -к) to indicate observed or certain past events.

examples.en: Сен бүгін таңғы асты іштің бе?

mistakes.note: The definite past uses Category-1 endings: the 1st person plural is '-қ/-к', not the present nominal ending '-быз/-біз'.
After a vowel stem ('оқы-'), the voiced affix '-ды' must be used, followed by the personal suffix '-м'.
Do not mix the participial past '-ған/-ген' with the definite past suffix '-ді'.

quiz.question: Which form means 'We wrote'?
quiz.explanation: The past definite tense for 'біз' takes the tense suffix '-ды' plus the Category-1 plural ending '-қ', yielding 'жаздық'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Сен кеше кімді көр___?' (Whom did you see yesterday?)
quiz.explanation: 'Сен' (informal 2nd person singular) requires the ending '-ң', hence 'көрдің'.

quiz.question: How do you conjugate 'кет-' (to leave) for 'Мен' in definite past?
quiz.explanation: Because 'кет-' ends in voiceless 'т', the suffix assimilates to voiceless '-ті-', followed by '-м': 'кеттім'.

quiz.question: What is the third-person singular form of 'айту' (to say) in definite past?
quiz.explanation: Third-person singular takes no personal suffix after the tense marker: 'айт-' + '-ты' = 'айтты'.

tip: Category-1 personal endings used here are identical to the possessive endings on nouns: -м (my/I), -ң (your/you), -қ/-к (our/we).

title: Habitual Present and Probable Future (-а/-е/-й)
subtitle: Expressing routines, general truths, and future intentions
keyPoint: Attach -а / -е after consonant stems and -й after vowel stems, followed by Category-2 personal endings (-мын, -сың, -ды) to express habits or planned futures.

examples.en: Сен де бізбен бірге шай ішесің бе?
Олар бүгін келмейді, өйткені бос емес.

mistakes.note: Use the -а/-е/-й tense for future intentions; auxiliary verbs like 'жатыр' indicate continuous actions happening right now.
When the stem already ends in 'и' or a vowel, the suffix merges into '-й' (or contracts to '-иды'), avoid '-иады'.
The first-person plural Category-2 suffix is '-мыз/-міз' directly attached to the tense suffix, yielding 'барамыз'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'I go to work every day'?
quiz.explanation: Habitual daily action takes the -а/-е/-й suffix with the 1st person ending: 'барамын'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Ол ертең саған телефон соғ___.' (He will call you tomorrow.)
quiz.explanation: The third-person ending for consonant-final stems in this tense is '-ады / -еді'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct negative form: 'I will not come tomorrow.'
quiz.explanation: The negative marker '-ме-' ends in a vowel, taking '-й' + 1st person ending '-мін' -> 'келмеймін'.

quiz.question: What is the correct 1st person plural form: 'Біз ертең емтихан тапсыр___'?
quiz.explanation: The 1st-person plural ending is '-мыз/-міз'; after hard stem 'тапсыр-' + '-а', it produces 'тапсырамыз'.

tip: Context resolves ambiguity: with time words like 'күнде' (daily) this tense is habitual present; with 'ертең' (tomorrow) it operates as the future tense.

title: Coordinating and Linking Converbs (-p and -a/-e/-y)
subtitle: Chain consecutive or simultaneous actions smoothly into one sentence
keyPoint: Use the suffix -(ы)п/-(і)п to link actions happening in sequence, and -а/-е/-й to express simultaneous or continuous background actions.

cells: Hard stem + а, Soft stem + е

examples.en: Ол таңғы ас ішіп, жұмысқа кетті.
Біз кітапханаға барып, көп кітап алдық.
Олар сөйлесейік деп шай іше отырды.

mistakes.wrong: Мен шай іштім және жұмыс істедім.
mistakes.note: Kazakh naturally prefers converbs like -(ы)п over repeating finite verbs with 'және' (and).
To show repeated simultaneous continuous action with consonant/vowel harmony, use -а/-е/-й rather than mixing standard past chains.
The suffix -(ы)п follows standard fourfold vowel harmony; 'оқы-' takes '-п' directly after a vowel stem.

quiz.question: Complete the sequence: 'Үйге ___ тамақ пісірдім.' (I came home and cooked)
quiz.explanation: The converb -іп shows the completed first action in a sequential chain.

quiz.question: Choose the simultaneous action: 'Ол күлімдей ___ жауап берді.' (She answered smiling)
quiz.explanation: The converb in -а/-е expresses the ongoing manner or simultaneous state during the main action.

quiz.question: Connect 'жазу' (to write) to express 'Wrote and sent': 'Хат ___ жіберді.'
quiz.explanation: A consonant-ending stem takes -ып/-іп (жаз- + -ып = жазып).

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly chains multiple actions?
quiz.explanation: 'Келіп, бәрін көрді' is natural Kazakh syntax using the sequential converb.

tip: Only the final verb in a converb chain receives tense and personal agreement endings; all preceding chained verbs take -п or -а/-е/-й.

title: Imperative and Optative Moods Across Formality Registers
subtitle: Command, request, and propose actions across informal, polite, and formal registers
keyPoint: Use bare stems for informal commands (сен), add -(ы)ңыз/-(і)ңіз for polite singular (сіз), and use -(а/е)йық for first-person cohortative proposals ('let's').

mistakes.note: Addressing 'Сіз' with an informal bare stem is considered rude; always append -(ы)ңыз/-(і)ңіз.
To propose 'Let us go together', use the optative/cohortative -айық/-ейік, not the plain indicative future.
Do not mix plural formal endings with the singular informal pronoun 'сен'.

quiz.question: Politely ask your teacher to enter: 'Төрге ___.'
quiz.explanation: The suffix -(і)ңіз creates the polite 2nd person (Сіз) imperative.

quiz.question: Invite a friend to eat lunch together: 'Түскі ас ___.'
quiz.explanation: The optative suffix -ейік conveys 'let us do' for the 1st person plural.

quiz.question: Give an informal command to a child: 'Тісіңді ___!'
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person singular informal (сен) takes the uninflected bare verb stem.

quiz.question: Formally address an audience: 'Сұрақтарыңызды ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Сіздер' (formal plural) takes -(ы)ңыздар / -(і)ңіздер.

tip: Attach -шы/-ші to any imperative stem (e.g., келші, келіңізші) to soften commands into warm, polite requests.

title: Aspectual Compound Verbs (Qal-, Ket-, Bast-, Ber-)
subtitle: Alter nuance, suddenness, and duration by chaining lexical roots with auxiliary verbs
keyPoint: Attach -(ы)п to the primary lexical verb and inflect auxiliary verbs like қалу (sudden state), кету (completion/departure), or беру (continuity) to modify aspect.

mistakes.note: The primary verb must take the converb form -(ы)п/-(і)п, never a finite past tense ending.
The inchoative auxiliary 'бастау' pairs with the -а/-е/-й converb, not -(ы)п.
Stacking incompatible aspectual auxiliaries distorts meaning; use specific auxiliaries like 'тастау' for decisive completion.

quiz.question: Express that someone fell asleep accidentally: 'Ол шаршап, диванда ___.'
quiz.explanation: The auxiliary 'қалу' after -(ы)п conveys unexpected or unplanned states.

quiz.question: Indicate that a train suddenly departed: 'Пойыз станциядан ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Жүріп кету' marks rapid or decisive departure.

quiz.question: Express the start of an event: 'Қар ___.' (It started snowing)
quiz.explanation: 'Бастау' selects the -а/-е converb to express the beginning of an event.

quiz.question: Tell someone to continue speaking without hesitation: 'Сөзіңді тоқтатпай, ___.'
quiz.explanation: Converb -а/-е + 'беру' indicates continuing the action freely without pause.

tip: Pay attention to the linking converb: 'бастау' and 'беру' take -а/-е/-й, while 'қалу', 'кету', and 'тастау' take -(ы)п/-(і)п.

title: Evidential and Resultative Past Tenses (-qan/-gen and -(y)pty)
subtitle: Distinguish between direct witness, inferential conclusions, and heard reports
keyPoint: Use -ды/-ді for personally witnessed facts, -(ы)пты/-(і)пті for unwitnessed surprise/hearsay, and -ған/-ген for established resultative past states.

cells: Apparently came / Turns out he came
Has come / Came in the past

mistakes.wrong: Мен кеше оны көрдім, ол келіпті.
mistakes.right: Мен кеше оны көрдім, ол келді.
mistakes.note: If you witnessed the event directly with your own eyes, use the witnessed past -ды/-ді.
Do not merge the participial past -ған with the indicative witnessed past -ды on the same stem.
The hearsay/realization suffix on consonant stems is -ыпты/-іпті, directly attached to the stem.

quiz.question: You look outside and notice puddles: 'Түнде жаңбыр ___.' (Apparently it rained)
quiz.explanation: -(ы)пты expresses an inference or realization based on observable aftermath.

quiz.question: Confirming your own direct lifelong experience: 'Мен Түркияда ___.' (I have been to Turkey)
quiz.explanation: The resultative past -ған/-ген combined with personal endings marks past experience.

quiz.question: Reporting gossip you heard second-hand: 'Ербол үйлен___.' (They say Yerbol got married)
quiz.explanation: -(і)пті denotes hearsay or second-hand information without direct observation.

quiz.question: Which verb explicitly states direct personal eyewitness?
quiz.explanation: -ды/-ді specifically denotes events directly witnessed by the speaker.

tip: Think of -(ы)пты as 'Aha! Apparently...' or 'I hear that...'; it signals that you did not see the action occur firsthand.

title: Verbal Nouns (-u) and Relative Participles (-qan, -atyn)
subtitle: Nominalize verbal actions and build relative clauses modifying head nouns
keyPoint: Use -у to turn verbs into nouns that decline with case endings, and place participles (-ған past, -атын habitual) directly before nouns to create relative clauses.

mistakes.note: Verbal nouns in -у act like real nouns and must take the accusative suffix (-ді/-ды) before transitive verbs like 'жақсы көру'.

mistakes.wrong: Кісі кім келді кеше менің досым.
mistakes.note: Kazakh does not use relative pronouns like 'who/which'; the participle directly precedes the noun it modifies.

mistakes.wrong: Ол оқитын кітапты кеше сатып алды келген.
mistakes.right: Ол кеше келген кітапты сатып алды.
mistakes.note: Keep participial relative clauses strictly positioned immediately before the noun they modify.

quiz.question: Express: 'Learning a language is important.' -> 'Тіл ___ маңызды.'
quiz.explanation: The verbal noun ending -у nominalizes the verb stem 'үйрен-' into 'learning'.

quiz.question: Choose the relative clause: 'The boy who read the book.' -> 'Кітапты ___ бала.'
quiz.explanation: The past participle -ған modifies 'бала' to mean 'the boy who read'.

quiz.question: Describe regular habit: 'The train that leaves every morning.' -> 'Әр таңда ___ пойыз.'
quiz.explanation: -атын/-етін forms habitual participles modifying nouns for repeated or general actions.

quiz.question: Add the correct accusative case to the verbal noun: 'Ол көлік ___ үйренді.' (He learned driving a car)
quiz.explanation: The direct object of 'үйренді' requires the accusative case suffix (-ді) on the verbal noun 'жүргізу'.

tip: Because Kazakh is head-final, put the entire relative modifier (clause + participle) before the noun it describes, with zero relative pronouns.

title: Conditional Mood (-sa/-se) and Temporal Clauses
subtitle: Expressing hypothetical conditions and 'when' clauses in Kazakh
keyPoint: Attach the suffix -sa or -se directly to the verb stem followed by personal endings to express 'if' or temporal 'when'.

cells: if it rains / when it rains

useCases.label: Real Condition
useCases.example: Ертең күн ашық болса, саябаққа барамыз.

mistakes.note: Kazakh does not use indicative future tense for conditions; the conditional suffix -sa/-se is required on the verb.
The conditional suffix must take person agreement markers corresponding to the subject.
Third person conditional takes no personal ending; do not append -ды/-ді.

quiz.question: If you (informal) come tomorrow, we will talk.
quiz.explanation: The second person singular informal ending is -ң, making 'келсең' the correct form.

quiz.question: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
quiz.explanation: The third person singular subject takes the bare conditional suffix -sa without personal endings.

quiz.question: If we buy the book, we can read it together.
quiz.explanation: The first person plural ending is -қ/-к, yielding 'алсақ'.

quiz.question: If I finish early, I will call you.
quiz.explanation: The first person singular requires the personal ending -м, so 'бітірсем' is correct.

tip: Even though the conjunction 'егер' (if) exists, it is optional and stylistic; the suffix -sa/-se on the verb is essential.

title: Modality of Necessity and Ability (-u kerek and -(a) al-)
subtitle: Expressing necessity with керек and capability with аламын
keyPoint: Combine verbal noun suffix -u with possessive suffixes and керек/қажет for necessity, or verb stem + -(a/e/y) with алу for ability.

useCases.label: Learned Skill
useCases.example: Ол қазақ тілінде еркін сөйлей алады.

useCases.label: Physical Possibility
useCases.example: Сіз мына ауыр қорапты көтере аласыз ба?

examples.en: Бізге жаңа ережені жақсылап түсіну керек.

mistakes.right: Маған бару керек. / Менің баруым керек.
mistakes.note: With 'керек', the agent must take either the dative case (маған) or genitive case with a possessive suffix on the verbal noun (менің баруым).
Ability with 'алу' requires the converb suffix (-а/-е/-й), not the verbal noun (-у).
Do not conjugate the main lexical verb before the auxiliary verb 'алу'.

quiz.question: I have to leave right now.
quiz.explanation: 'кетуім керек' combines verbal noun -у + 1st person possessive -ім + керек to mean 'I must leave'.

quiz.question: Can you (informal) speak English?
quiz.explanation: 'сөйлей аласың ба' properly uses converb -й + auxiliary verb 'алу' in the question form.

quiz.question: We must complete this work today.
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural possessive marker is -іміз, forming 'бітіруіміз керек'.

quiz.question: He cannot swim.
quiz.explanation: Negative ability combines converb -е with 'алмайды', yielding 'жүзе алмайды'.

tip: To express inability or negative capacity, negate the auxiliary 'алу' (e.g. алмаймын, алмадым) rather than the main verb.

title: Voice Derivations: Causative and Passive
subtitle: Deriving causative (-тыр/-гіз/-ыр) and passive (-ыл/-ын) verb stems
keyPoint: Kazakh modifies verb valency by suffixing causative markers to make someone do an action, or passive markers (-ыл/-іл/-л) to demote the subject.

mistakes.right: Кітап мен тарапымнан оқылды. / Кітап оқылды.
mistakes.note: Passive verbs do not take an agent in the nominative case; omit the agent or use 'тарапынан'.
To say 'I made my child read', use causative -т (оқыт-), not base verb (оқы-).
Passive -ыл denotes an action done to a subject, while reflexive -ын denotes self-directed action.

quiz.question: The door was opened quietly.
quiz.explanation: The passive form of ашу (to open) is 'ашылу', in past tense 'ашылды'.

quiz.question: The teacher made the students write an essay.
quiz.explanation: The causative form of жазу (to write) is 'жазғызу', so 'жазғызды' expresses having someone write.

quiz.question: The meeting will be held tomorrow.
quiz.explanation: 'өткізіледі' combines causative өткіз- with passive -іл- to mean 'will be conducted/held'.

quiz.question: He got dressed and went out.
quiz.explanation: Reflexive -ін is used for actions performed on oneself, forming 'киінді' (got dressed).

tip: In causative sentences, the secondary agent (the person caused to perform the action) takes the dative case (-ға/-ге/-қа/-ке).

title: Complex Converbial Clauses (-ғанша, -ғалы, -ғандықтан)
subtitle: Subordinating clauses expressing time limits, starting points, and causality
keyPoint: Participles (-ған/-ген) combine with dative, ablative, or lexical postpositions to build complex subordinate clauses of limit, duration, and reason.

useCases.label: Time Limit ('until')
useCases.example: Мен келгенше, осы жерде күте тұрыңыз.

useCases.label: Logical Cause ('because')
useCases.example: Ауа райы бұзылғандықтан, сапар кейінге қалды.

mistakes.note: The suffix -ғанша/-генше already includes the limitative meaning 'until'; adding 'дейін' is redundant.

mistakes.wrong: Оны көрген бері бес жыл өтті.
mistakes.right: Оны көргелі бері бес жыл өтті.
mistakes.note: 'Бері' governs the -ғалы/-гелі converb form or an ablative noun, not plain -ған.
Causal conjunction requires the ablative suffix -тан/-тен on the derived noun: -ғандықтан.

quiz.question: Wait here until I arrive.
quiz.explanation: The suffix -ғанша/-генше expresses 'until / up to the point of'.

quiz.question: It has been three years since we graduated from school.
quiz.explanation: -ғалы/-гелі indicates time elapsed since an initial action ('since graduating').

quiz.question: Since he was ill, he did not come to class.
quiz.explanation: -ғандықтан/-гендіктен expresses logical cause ('because / since he was ill').

quiz.question: Let's drink tea until the rain stops.
quiz.explanation: 'until it stops' requires -ғанша, making 'басылғанша' correct.

tip: For negative 'since' constructions (e.g. 'I haven't seen you in ages'), attach -ғалы to the negative stem: 'көрмегелі'.

title: Reported Speech and Quotative Formations with 'De-'
subtitle: Embedding quotes, intentions, and thoughts using деп, деген, and десе
keyPoint: The verb деу (to say) forms the converb деп to mark direct speech, intentions, and subjective reasons in complex sentences.

cells: if you ask about the price

useCases.label: Direct/Indirect Quote
useCases.example: Мұғалім ертең сабақ болмайды деп айтты.

examples.en: Досыма сыйлық алайын деп дүкенге бардым.
Ол келмей қала ма деп қорықтым.
Жақсы оқысын деп баласына компьютер әперді.

mistakes.note: Kazakh cannot simply juxtapose clauses like English 'He said that...'; you must use the quotative converb 'деп'.

mistakes.wrong: Мен оған бару үшін деп ойладым.
mistakes.note: Intention with thought verbs pairs the voluntative/optative mood (-айын/-ейін) with 'деп'.

mistakes.wrong: Бір адам аты Арман деп келді.
mistakes.note: When introducing someone or something called by a name, use the participial form 'деген'.

quiz.question: He said: 'I understand everything'.
quiz.explanation: Quotations are linked to communication verbs via the converb 'деп'.

quiz.question: There is a city called Turkistan in southern Kazakhstan.
quiz.explanation: The participle 'деген' functions like 'called' or 'named' modifying a noun.

quiz.question: I went out intending to buy bread.
quiz.explanation: Intention before 'деп' requires the 1st person optative-voluntative suffix -айын/-ейін ('алайын деп').

quiz.question: She worried that she might be late.
quiz.explanation: Thoughts and apprehensions are quoted internally with '...деп қорықты / уайымдады'.

tip: Combine the 1st person optative (-айын/-ейін) with 'деп тұрмын' or 'деп жүрмін' to express an immediate future intention (e.g. айтайын деп тұрмын = I'm about to say).
